chosen_by.rule: The warehouse the farmer named, when they named one; else, among the nearest few of each operator, the one where storing leaves the most per quintal in a typical year after storage, loss and the trip there: first among those where the engine itself said store for some length (the best such length), then among those where storing can be counted at all (the best length); then one with a published rate for the crop; then the nearer (straight line), the cheaper rate, the operator and the name.

wastage.headline: This crop shrinks and can rot while it is stored.

published.text: STORAGE LOSES PART OF THE CROP: the ICAR onion and garlic institute says 30 to 40% of stored onion gets lost; up to 42% over four months in a thatched store and up to 46% in a ventilated one (about 55 to 59% in its 120-day trial of ventilated and bulk storage); 5% in a cold store at 0 °C, though 27% of those onions sprouted within 15 days of coming out; and 7.14% in the institute's own store kept at about 27 °C. These are the institute's statements and trials, not losses measured on farms in Nashik.
